questions.question: Before starting down a hill, you should:
questions.explanation: Shift into a lower gear before going downhill. Choose a speed that does not require heavy braking.

questions.question: After changing a tire, you should stop after driving a short distance to:

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Check that the tire tread is good.
Make sure the right tire was changed.
Check if rocks are in the tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: Stop a short time after changing a tire to check that the lug nuts are tight.

questions.question: When it is hard to see, such as at dawn or dusk, how do you make your vehicle more visible?
questions.explanation: When visibility is poor (at dawn, dusk, rain, or snow), turn on your low beam headlights to make your vehicle easier to see. Do not use high beams when other vehicles are near.

questions.question: When driving on a long downhill slope, you should brake by:

options.text: Using mostly brakes and sometimes downshifting.
Downshifting first, then using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Downshifting first, then using the brakes.
questions.explanation: Before going down a long hill, shift into a lower gear and then brake properly. Using only brakes can cause them to overheat and fail. The engine's braking power, which is stronger in a lower gear, is the main way to control your speed on a downhill.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, engine belts should be:

options.text: Inspected only if they look frayed.

questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check engine belts for tightness and wear.

questions.question: What can the crack-the-whip effect do?
questions.explanation: The crack-the-whip effect can cause a trailer to roll over during a lane change. Avoid this by changing lanes slowly and safely.

questions.question: When you need to stop in an emergency, you should:

options.text: Veer your trailer to the right and stop.
Veer your trailer to the left and stop.

questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, brake in a way that keeps your vehicle straight while still allowing you to turn if needed. You can use controlled braking or stab braking.

questions.question: When checking a coupling device, you should:

options.text: Look for mud on the fifth wheel.
Make sure the kingpin is polished.
Make sure there is space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.
Make sure the locking jaws are closed on the kingpin.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the locking jaws are closed on the kingpin.
questions.explanation: When checking a coupling device, make sure there is no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel. The locking jaws must be securely closed around the kingpin.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a type of retarder?
questions.explanation: Retarders help slow a vehicle and reduce brake use. The four types of retarders are exhaust, engine, hydraulic, and electric.

questions.question: When approaching a construction worker near the road, you should:

options.text: Wait until construction is finished before driving.

questions.explanation: In work zones, follow posted speed limits. Slow down even more when workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: When stopping a manual transmission vehicle, what should you do when the engine is near idle?
questions.explanation: When stopping a manual transmission vehicle, push in the clutch when the engine is near idle.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Cannot be used on vehicles transporting hazardous materials.
Can help drivers see a larger area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help drivers see a larger area.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are curved. They let drivers see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, objects appear smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: A tractor protection valve is:

options.text: A device that keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or has a bad leak.
A device that controls fuel levels.
A device that allows the battery to recharge efficiently.

questions.correctAnswerText: A device that keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or has a bad leak.
questions.explanation: On vehicles with air brakes, the tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer develops a bad leak or breaks away.

questions.question: Using an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) helps you stay in control during hard braking, but it does not always shorten your stopping distance.

questions.question: When driving, mirrors should be used:

options.text: Only when there may be a problem.

questions.explanation: You need to know what is around your vehicle at all times. Check your mirrors often while driving.

questions.question: While driving downhill, brake until you reach a speed that is ____ below your safe speed, then release the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: While driving downhill, hold the brake until your vehicle reaches a speed 5 mph below your safe speed. Then release the brake. Repeat this process.

questions.question: The weight of a truck:

options.text: Usually has no impact on stopping distance.
Is a major factor in stopping distance.
Is not as important as cargo type in stopping distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a major factor in stopping distance.
questions.explanation: A vehicle's weight is important for stopping distance. Heavier vehicles need more braking power to stop.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Move quickly, before other vehicles can enter the lane.
Move slowly in case another vehicle is in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move slowly in case another vehicle is in the lane.
questions.explanation: Change lanes slowly and smoothly. If there is another vehicle you did not see, they will have time to react.

questions.question: Looking far ahead when driving is:

options.text: Discouraged because the road ahead is not as important as your current location.
Encouraged to help you spot hazards early.
Only encouraged when transporting hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encouraged to help you spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: Look 12 to 15 seconds ahead of your vehicle. This lets you see hazards early and react with time to spare.

questions.question: You should ____ if the low pressure warning signal activates while driving.

options.text: Stop where you are and park
Exit the roadway as soon as safely possible

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the roadway as soon as safely possible
questions.explanation: If the low pressure warning signal activates, safely exit the roadway and park as soon as you can. Low air pressure means your brakes will not work well enough to stop safely.
